{{Top|Enemy|Grineer|Grineer|Weapon|Weapons|Weapons}} {{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic}} {{Codex|Detonate heads with this slow-firing rifle that rewards precision.}} The '''Kuva Chakkhurr''' is a unique [[Kuva (Variant)|Kuva]] flintlock-styled rifle. It fires explosive rounds that deal immense damage, even more so on headshots, at the expense of a low [[fire rate]], slow [[reload speed]], and limited ammo reserves. ==Characteristics== *This weapon deals primarily {{D|Impact}} damage. *Direct shots deals '''50%''' more [[Enemy_Body_Parts|headshot]] damage. *Shots explode in a '''2.9''' meter radius after impacting a surface or enemy. **Both initial hit and explosion have guaranteed {{D|Impact}} proc. **Initial hit and explosion apply status separately. **Explosion does not need direct line of sight to deal damage and will penetrate walls. **Can benefit from {{M|Firestorm}} ({{M|Primed Firestorm|Primed}}) and {{M|Cautious Shot}}. *Innate two {{Pol|Madurai}} polarities. *Adversary Weapon: **Comes with an additional bonus {{D|Impact}}, {{D|Heat}}, {{D|Cold}}, {{D|Electricity}}, {{D|Toxin}}, {{D|Magnetic}}, or {{D|Radiation}} damage, based on the Kuva Lich's [[Adversary System/Progenitor|progenitor Warframe]], which increases the listed base damage of the weapon by 25%-60%. ***[[Valence Fusion]] can optionally change the resulting output damage type, and can upgrade the bonus increase (up to 60%). **[[Polarization|Polarizing]] the weapon increases its max [[rank]] by '''2''', capping at rank '''40''' after '''5''' polarizations, granting the weapon additional mod capacity. **{{Resource|Elemental Vice}} can be applied to the weapon after it has reached rank 40, allowing the bonus damage type to be swapped freely. **Listed [[Mastery Rank]] requirement is not enforced - the weapon may theoretically be obtained at any mastery rank by acquiring and vanquishing a Kuva Lich that has this weapon equipped. {{Advantages|class=Rifle|trigger=Semi-Auto| *Highest base damage of all semi-automatic rifles. *Highest [[critical chance]] of semi-automatic rifles, and tied with {{Weapon|Nataruk}} , {{Weapon|Dread}} and {{Weapon|Lenz}} for highest critical chance of all weapons. *Pinpoint [[accuracy]] when aiming. }} {{Disadvantages|class=Rifle|trigger=Semi-Auto| *Slowest [[fire rate]] of all semi-automatic rifles. *Projectiles have travel time with slight arcing. *Inaccurate beyond short range when fired from the hip. *Explosion inflicts [[Stagger|self-stagger]]. *Explosion has a [[Enemy Body Parts|headshot]] multiplier of 1x and cannot trigger headshot conditions. *Explosion has linear [[Damage Falloff]] from 100% to 70% from central impact. }} ==Acquisition== {{Transclude|Adversary System/Weapons#Kuva Acquisition}} ==Notes== *The +50% bonus damage on headshots is additive to other sources of +bonus damage on headshot such as {{Arcane|Primary Deadhead}} and {{A|Prowl}}. {{Transclude|Adversary System#Notes}} {{Transclude|Adversary System/Progenitor}} ==Tips== *{{WF|Harrow}} is particularly well-suited for this weapon; {{A|Condemn}} can be used to hold enemies in place, {{A|Penance}} can mitigate the Kuva Chakkurr's slow fire rate and reload speed, and the bonus critical chance from {{A|Covenant}}, particularity the quadrupled bonus on headshots, can make easy work of clustered enemies. *{{WF|Sevagoth}} is also well-suited for the rifle, as {{A|Gloom}} will slow enemies down and will allow him to easily compensate for the projectile's lead time and land an easy headshot. *A Kuva Chakkhurr with bonus {{D|Radiation}} or {{D|Cold}} is a good choice for [[Eidolon Teralyst]] hunts, though the slow fire rate will have to be compensated for via modding and/or {{Arcane|Arcane Acceleration}}. *Because of its guaranteed {{D|Impact}} procs and slow fire rate, the Kuva Chakkhurr is well-suited to use {{M|Internal Bleeding}}. ==Trivia== *As mentioned above, the Kuva Chakkhurr is modeled after [[wikipedia:Flintlock|flintlock]] firearms, which operated by striking a piece of [[wikipedia:flint|flint]] on a steel plate, generating sparks that ignite gunpowder covered by the steel plate and discharging the round. Aspects of the Chakkhurr's design allude to this; **The most obvious instances are two levers on the Chakkhurr's receiver that swing forward every time it is fired, analogous to a flintlock's [[wikipedia:Hammer_(firearms)|hammer]], which held the flint. The use of gunpowder is also reflected with copious amounts of smoke created every time the Chakkhurr is fired. **The hook at the bottom of the barrel, which is largely ornamental, is based on the [[wikipedia:Ramrod|ramrod]], which was used during reloading to compress both the round and the gunpowder to improve the likelihood of a successful discharge. Reloading a flintlock was also a time-consuming process; the gunpowder and round were loaded from the muzzle then the ramrod was pushed up the barrel. This serves as the basis of the Chakkhurr's slow reload speed. **Some armies used [[wikipedia:Paper cartridge|paper cartridges]], which had pre-measured amounts of gunpowder and had portions tied off with thread to speed up reloading, and these portions would be untied to first use the gunpowder. The Chakkhurr's reload animation consists of pulling the string to release the old magazine and pulling it again to secure the fresh magazine. *Whenever the Kuva Chakkhurr is fired into a large enough space, such as a [[Landscape]] mission, the shot will be followed by the sound of a bullet cutting through the air; a feature currently unique to the Chakkhurr {{Cite}}. *"Chakkhurr" is an onomatopoeia for flintlock rifles. "Chak" for the flint knapped striker striking the steel frizzen (steel downward part of a flintlock rifle, to create a spark), and the "khurr" for the resulting fiery, slow gunpowder explosion. ==Bugs== *If a shot is fired off at the same time when using Mesa's Peacemaker, then it will make the Kuva Chakkhurr automatically hit one target without having to aim. {{Cite}} ==Media== Kuva Chakkhurr 1.png|Kuva Chakkhurr when equipped in the arsenal Kuva Chakkhurr 2.png {{VideoGallery |{{YouTube|0_s8jKcodFw|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|831DEekLokM|size=300px}} }} {{SkinGallery}} ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|32}} ;Ammo Changes We understand the power fantasy of these weapons is very popular for some, so our first approach was to keep them powerful, but limit how often they can be used by making changes to ammo pick-up. '''''Ammo Pickup Overrides'''''
The following weapons now have ammo pickup overrides, meaning they gain less from picking up ammo. This mostly applies to AoE weapons, in hopes that players will become more deliberate with their aim to make the most of their Ammo pools. The following lists the specific ammo pick up overrides per weapon category. '''Primary Weapon Ammo Pick Up Overrides''' 15 Ammo per Pick Up: *Kuva Chakkhurr ;Headshot Damage Changes During playtesting, the ammo changes alone weren’t enough to significantly change things for AoE weapons. So instead of tightening these values to be overly restrictive, we chose to address other factors that make these weapons so strong, such as headshot damage. Our approach here is two-fold, to reduce the impact of headshots for AOE weapons, but to also make precision headshots pack a larger punch overall. *Radial damage no longer gains extra headshot damage or triggers headshot conditions. **This is primarily targeted at the Ignis Wraith - as a “flamethrower” weapon, it’s hard to imagine a blanket of elements being precise enough to target weak points specifically. Explosive projectiles themselves can still land headshots, so there is still a reason to aim with most weapons for maximum damage. {{ver|27.2.2}}
Reduced the following AoE weapons Radial Damage Falloff from central impact that were all previously 90%: *Kuva Chakkhurr: 30% {{ver|27.2.1}} *Decreased the distance to point of impact that Self Stagger is inflicted with the Shedu due to having a large AoE range. {{ver|27.2}} ;Self Damage Changes: We are getting rid of Self Damage and replacing it with something else: instead of Self Damage, it’s now ‘Stagger’. This change completely removes the chance of killing yourself, and instead now creates scenarios where you will interrupt yourself - or ‘Stagger’ - to varying degrees if you aren’t careful. The degrees of Self-Interrupt start with a small stumble all the way to full knockdown depending on how close you are to the center of explosion. Any Mods referring to Self Damage will be converted to acknowledge Stagger. With this Self-Interrupt system, we have added dozens of new recovery animations that harness a ninja-like recovery experience. By pressing ‘Jump’ at the correct time, you can execute a ninja-skill-based knockdown recovery to ALL in-game knockdowns. This ninja recovery window is indicated by a glowing FX on your Warframe. In addition to Self Damage being removed, some of the more powerful AOE weapons without Self Damage presently will have the Stagger added, but it should only be noticeable in cases of extreme inaccuracy on the player’s part. The Weapons include: *Kuva Chakkhurr In the original Dev Workshop, we said:
''As a result of this overall systemic change, Weapons with Stagger will be getting approximately a 20% buff in Damage, with any weapons with AOE receiving a 50% Radial Damage Falloff from central impact.'' This is no longer accurate after continued testing. What we are doing now is: No damage buffs have been added, but any weapons with AOE are receiving ~20% increase in Radius. Additionally, AOE weapons are receiving a 90% Radial Damage Falloff from central impact. This means on the very outer section of the explosion Radius 10% of the Damage will be dealt. Tactics will be deadly - aim true, Tenno. ''Why: Several players brought up the history of the Tonkor and we want to make sure we ship this change in a place that’s conservative in its starting point from a balance perspective. The complete removal of Self Damage does change the pace of destruction with some of the game’s most powerful weapons, so we want to make sure we can iterate upwardly instead of releasing a bonanza of explosions with no other choices.'' {{ver|26.0.7}} *Explosion damage changed from 106 Blast to 106 (50 Puncture, 36 Slash, and 20 Blast) (undocumented). *Fixed Kuva Lich weapons that do damage on both impact and explosion (Kuva Ogris, Kuva Ayanga, etc) doing significantly less overall damage than expected. This was due to the Elemental bonus only being applied to the "on impact" of the projectile itself and not the explosion. {{ver|26}} *Introduced. }} {{WeaponNav}} [[es:Chakkhurr Kuva]] [[Category:Update 26]] [[Category:Weapons]] [[Category:Grineer]] [[Category:Self Interrupt Weapons]] [[uk:Чакхур-кува]]

Even missions with low enemy density will drop plenty of ammo to keep your Kuva Ogris well-supplied. *Installing {{M|Nightwatch Napalm}} grants the Kuva Ogris an effective crowd control capability, as the lingering flames deal {{D|Heat}} damage which procs Heat status, briefly stunning those who are affected. **As [[Railjack]] [[Railjack/Crew|Crewmates]] use player weapons ''with their mod configurations'', handing them a Kuva Ogris with Nightwatch Napalm makes them a crucial crowd control support when needed, as they can sustain the lingering flames indefinitely, since they do not need ammo. **{{A|Toxic Lash}} will apply {{D|Toxin}} damage, and a guaranteed Toxin status, every time [[Nightwatch Napalm]] damages an enemy. {{Top|Enemy|Grineer|Grineer}} {{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic}} {{codex|The Kuva Drakgoon flak cannon sends volleys of intensely hot shrapnel ricocheting around the room that do not slow down. Larger Magazine Capacity and Reload Speed. Can be fired in wide or concentrated bursts.}} The '''Kuva Drakgoon''' is the [[Kuva (Variant)|Kuva]] variant of the {{Weapon|Drakgoon}} flak cannon, featuring a larger magazine, faster reload speed, faster charge time, and much higher critical chance on charged shots, but at some expense to base damage. ==Characteristics== *This weapon does primarily {{D|Slash}} damage. *Shots [[Bounce]] once. **This allows one to fire at a wall and kill an enemy behind cover, albeit with some difficulty. **Shrapnel does not slow down after bouncing. *Charged shots have innate 1.5 meter [[punch through]]. *Innate [[multishot]] of 10 pellets. *Effective over multiple ranges due to charge/spread mechanic: **Uncharged shots fires wide-dispersal shots to soften up multiple enemies at mid/long range, or quickly hit a single target at short range. **Charged shots fires a tightly focused blast over longer ranges for high single-target damage. *Can use the Drakgoon-exclusive {{M|Fomorian Accelerant}} mod. *Adversary Weapon: **Comes with an additional bonus {{D|Impact}}, {{D|Heat}}, {{D|Cold}}, {{D|Electricity}}, {{D|Toxin}}, {{D|Magnetic}}, or {{D|Radiation}} damage, based on the Kuva Lich's [[Adversary System/Progenitor|progenitor Warframe]], which increases the listed base damage of the weapon by 25%-60%. ***[[Valence Fusion]] can optionally change the resulting output damage type, and can upgrade the bonus increase (up to 60%). **[[Polarization|Polarizing]] the weapon increases its max [[rank]] by '''2''', capping at rank '''40''' after '''5''' polarizations, granting the weapon additional mod capacity. **{{Resource|Elemental Vice}} can be applied to the weapon after it has reached rank 40, allowing the bonus damage type to be swapped freely. **Listed [[Mastery Rank]] requirement is not enforced - the weapon may theoretically be obtained at any mastery rank by acquiring and vanquishing a Kuva Lich that has this weapon equipped. {{Advantages|class=Shotgun| *Very fast charge speed. *No damage falloff. }} {{Disadvantages|class=Shotgun| *Shrapnel projectiles have travel time. }} {{WeaponComparison|Drakgoon}} ==Acquisition== {{Transclude|Adversary System/Weapons#Kuva Acquisition}} ==Notes== {{Transclude|Adversary System#Notes}} {{Transclude|Adversary System/Progenitor}} *Despite the lower base damage, with the minimum elemental damage bonus of 25%, and increased critical stats, the Kuva Drakgoon will deal more damage on average for charged shots than the original Drakgoon. And a damage bonus of over {{Math|(400)(1+0.075(2.0-1))/(1+0.21(2.5-1))/230 - 1|p=y}} will cause the uncharged shot to deal more damage on average as well. This is accounting only for base critical hit stats; the higher status chance will also increase status-based damage. **Any mods that enhance critical hit chance or damage will increase the advantage of the Kuva Drakgoon over the original. **Because the Kuva Drakgoon has the same status chance for charged vs uncharged shots and the Drakgoon has a lower status chance on uncharged shots, the uncharged shot on the Kuva Drakgoon will deal more status-based damage. **Important to note however is due to a lower Riven disposition, Damage and Multishot riven mods will allow the standard Drakgoon to obtain ''significantly'' higher base damage, though lacking the critical power of the Kuva version, making non crit shots deal more damage on the normal variant. ==Trivia== *The Grineer text on the right side of the weapon reads "WRECK". It is mirrored on the left side. *Going by the structure of the Grineer language and the function of the weapon, the name "Drakgoon" is most likely meant to translate to "Flakgun" ==Media== Kuva Drakgoon 1.png|Kuva Drakgoon, as shown in the arsenal Kuva Drakgoon 2.png {{SkinGallery}} ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|32}} ;Ammo Changes We understand the power fantasy of these weapons is very popular for some, so our first approach was to keep them powerful, but limit how often they can be used by making changes to ammo pick-up. '''''Ammo Pickup Overrides'''''
The following weapons now have ammo pickup overrides, meaning they gain less from picking up ammo. This mostly applies to AoE weapons, in hopes that players will become more deliberate with their aim to make the most of their Ammo pools. The following lists the specific ammo pick up overrides per weapon category. '''Primary Weapon Ammo Pick Up Overrides''' 15 Ammo per Pick Up: *Kuva Drakgoon {{ver|29.6.6}} *Fixed equipping Unreal Skins to Kuva weapons overriding their stats to perform like their base version. {{ver|27.2}} ;Greater than 100% Status having meaning: Shotguns have a unique Role here based on a very patch-work history with how they interact with Status Chance. A Shotgun that shoots 99% Status Chance would give you 35% (roughly) status per pellet. 100% Status Gives you 100% Status per pellet. This huge jump in performance happens with just a 1% gain - why? Well, to answer that we have to look at our choice to make what the UI conveys reality. It would feel broken to shoot a Shotgun with 100% Status and not see a perfect spread of Effects. In reality, to make Status consistent we have to treat Shotguns as a special case. Shotguns as a special case means we have buffed the Status Chance of all Shotguns by x3 or greater. The UI now behaves to show the reality that you are determining Status Chance per pellet. *(Undocumented) Status chance per projectile increased from 3% to 9%. {{ver|26}} *Introduced. }} ==See also== *{{Weapon|Drakgoon}}, the normal counterpart of this weapon. {{WeaponNav}} [[es:Drakgoon Kuva]] [[Category:Weapons]] [[Category:Primary Weapons]] [[Category:Shotgun]] [[Category:Update 26]] [[uk:Дракґун-кува]]

{{Top|Enemy|Grineer|Grineer|Weapon|Weapons|Weapons}} {{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic}} {{Codex|This Grineer bow delivers vengeance in the form of cluster bomb-tipped arrows that can be detonated mid-air or on impact. Low quiver capacity, arrows are recovered singly.}} The '''Kuva Bramma''' is a massive [[Kuva (Variant)|Kuva]] bow, firing arrows that produce a large {{D|Blast}} explosion on impact while also depositing cluster bombs, and is able to detonate mid-flight with [[Alternate Fire]], but suffers from small ammo capacity. ==Characteristics== *This weapon deals primarily {{D|Blast}} damage. *Cannot fire unless fully charged. *Shots explode in a '''8.3''' meter radius on impact with a surface or enemy, then splits into '''3''' smaller bomblets that rain down on the point of impact which explode in a '''3.5''' meter radius. **[[Alternate Fire]] prematurely detonates the arrow, and any bomblets, mid-flight. **Initial hit and explosion apply status separately. **Explosion does not need direct line of sight to deal damage and will penetrate walls. **Can benefit from {{M|Firestorm}} ({{M|Primed Firestorm|Primed}}) and {{M|Cautious Shot}}. **Can equip the bow-exclusive {{M|Thunderbolt}} mod. **{{M|Heavy Caliber}}'s [[accuracy]] penalty is minimal on this weapon. *[[Fire rate]] mods apply double their bonuses. *Innate {{Pol|Madurai}} polarity. *Adversary Weapon: **Comes with an additional bonus {{D|Impact}}, {{D|Heat}}, {{D|Cold}}, {{D|Electricity}}, {{D|Toxin}}, {{D|Magnetic}}, or {{D|Radiation}} damage, based on the Kuva Lich's [[Adversary System/Progenitor|progenitor Warframe]], which increases the listed base damage of the weapon by 25%-60%. ***[[Valence Fusion]] can optionally change the resulting output damage type, and can upgrade the bonus increase (up to 60%). **[[Polarization|Polarizing]] the weapon increases its max [[rank]] by '''2''', capping at rank '''40''' after '''5''' polarizations, granting the weapon additional mod capacity. **{{Resource|Elemental Vice}} can be applied to the weapon after it has reached rank 40, allowing the bonus damage type to be swapped freely. **Listed [[Mastery Rank]] requirement is not enforced - the weapon may theoretically be obtained at any mastery rank by acquiring and vanquishing a Kuva Lich that has this weapon equipped. {{Advantages|class=Bow| *Highest base damage of all bows. *Second fastest charge speed of all bows, behind {{Weapon|Rakta Cernos}}. }} {{Disadvantages|class=Bow| *Projectile has travel time with heavy arcing. *Relatively high spread, making aiming at distant targets inconsistent. *Extremely poor ammo economy: **Smallest ammo reserve of all bows at 5 rounds. **Only restores 1 unit of ammunition per ammo pickup. *[[Noise Level|Alarming]] unlike most bows, making it ill-suited for stealth gameplay. *Explosion and bomblets inflicts [[Stagger|self-stagger]]. *Explosion and bomblets have a [[Enemy Body Parts|headshot]] multiplier of 1x and cannot trigger headshot conditions. *Explosion has linear [[Damage Falloff]] from 100% to 10% from central impact. *Bomblets have linear damage falloff from 100% to 50% from central impact. }} ==Acquisition== {{Transclude|Adversary System/Weapons#Kuva Acquisition}} ==Notes== *Arrows fired by {{WF|Mirage}}'s {{A|Hall of Mirrors}} cannot detonate prematurely with [[Alternate Fire]]. *When used with {{WF|Ivara}}'s {{A|Navigator}} only the main hit and the radial damage get the damage multiplier, the droplets do not.[potential bug] *Can use {{M|Sniper Ammo Mutation}} and {{M|Primed Sniper Ammo Mutation}}, despite not being a sniper rifle. *{{WF|Cyte-09}}'s {{A|Resupply}} instantly restores the weapon's arrow reserve. Ammo packs produced by Resupply are not affected by the ammo drop override, and will also restore multiple arrows. {{Transclude|Adversary System#Notes}} {{Transclude|Adversary System/Progenitor}} ==Tips== *The weapon's low ammo economy can be mitigated with {{M|Arrow Mutation}}/{{M|Vigilante Supplies}}, {{M|Ammo Drum}}, and/or {{Companion|Carrier}}'s {{M|Ammo Case}}, and/or {{WF|Cyte-09}}'s {{A|Resupply}}. *The arcane {{Arcane|Primary Compression}} works extremedly well on this weapon, being the one that seems to benefit the most from all the primary AoE weapons in game by giving more damage than {{Arcane|Primary Merciless}} ==Trivia== *This weapon's name is derived from the ''[[wikipedia:Brahmastra|Brahmastra]]'', powerful weapons in [[wikipedia:Hindu Mythology|Hindu Mythology]] said to have been forged by the deity [[wikipedia:Brahma|Brahma]]. The Brahmastra are commonly depicted as arrows and are capable of utterly destroying whatever they hit. ==Bugs== *When using ''any'' arrow skin for the Kuva Bramma, the player will hold the arrows by the middle of their shaft rather than the end, causing the arrow tips to not even connect to the bow when fully charged. The following weapons now have ammo pickup overrides, meaning they gain less from picking up ammo. This mostly applies to AoE weapons, in hopes that players will become more deliberate with their aim to make the most of their Ammo pools. The following lists the specific ammo pick up overrides per weapon category. '''Primary Weapon Ammo Pick Up Overrides''' 1 Ammo per Pick Up: *Kuva Bramma ;Headshot Damage Changes During playtesting, the ammo changes alone weren’t enough to significantly change things for AoE weapons. So instead of tightening these values to be overly restrictive, we chose to address other factors that make these weapons so strong, such as headshot damage. Our approach here is two-fold, to reduce the impact of headshots for AOE weapons, but to also make precision headshots pack a larger punch overall. *Radial damage no longer gains extra headshot damage or triggers headshot conditions. **This is primarily targeted at the Ignis Wraith - as a “flamethrower” weapon, it’s hard to imagine a blanket of elements being precise enough to target weak points specifically. Explosive projectiles themselves can still land headshots, so there is still a reason to aim with most weapons for maximum damage. {{ver|32.0.1}} *Fixed the Kuva Bramma having a line of sight check on AoEs beyond 4m. **''This was a result of an experimental change not being reverted for launch, as discussed on the Devstream.'' {{ver|31.5}} *Fixed Wukong Clone holding the Kuva Bramma arrow incorrectly. {{ver|29.6.5}} *Fixed visual issues with the Oscira Bow Skin when equipped on the Kuva Bramma. {{ver|29.2.1}} *Fixed the Oscira Bow Skin not applying correctly to the Kuva Bramma. {{ver|28.3}} *Fixed arrows being misplaced when equipping the Dryad Bow Skin on the Kuva Bramma. {{ver|28}}
The Kuva Bramma has received balance changes to address it’s overwhelming chart topping usage. The Kuva Bramma still goes boom, and we look forward to your feedback once you’ve given it a try. Full detail can be found here: https://forums.warframe.com/topic/1199010-kuva-bramma-changes-explanation-and-timeline/ *It has a smaller reserve ammo (15 to 5), and gains fewer arrows from ammo pickups - This is to encourage players to aim the bow deliberately at crowds of enemies and not fire it wildly everywhere. *Fewer cluster bombs are produced on impact (from 7 to 3) - Reduces the overwhelming AOE potential somewhat but also makes the Bramma less visually busy. Players have said that the many many explosions produced by Bramma are hard to see through. *Increased cluster projectile radial attack size from 2.7m to 3.5m. *Reduced cluster projectile fall off from 100% to 50% - Fewer explosive fragments, but they cover more area and generally do more damage. *Updated the Kuva Bramnma description to include these changes: **''This Grineer bow delivers vengeance in the form of cluster bomb-tipped arrows that can be detonated mid-air or on impact. Low quiver capacity, arrows are recovered singly.'' {{ver|27.4}} *Fixed the Kuva Bramma’s projectiles not getting pulled into Mag’s Magnetize and instead bouncing off of the area and yeeting into the sky. {{ver|27.2.2}} *Removed unnecessary dud grenade FX on the Kuva Bramma cluster bombs. {{ver|27.2}} ;Kuva Lich Changes & Fixes: *Fixed the Kuva Bramma weapon progression showing as complete in the Codex when at Rank 30 instead of it’s true completed Rank of 40. *Fixed small FX offset issues with the Kuva Bramma when reloading. ;Self Damage Changes: We are getting rid of Self Damage and replacing it with something else: instead of Self Damage, it’s now ‘Stagger’. This change completely removes the chance of killing yourself, and instead now creates scenarios where you will interrupt yourself - or ‘Stagger’ - to varying degrees if you aren’t careful. The degrees of Self-Interrupt start with a small stumble all the way to full knockdown depending on how close you are to the center of explosion. Any Mods referring to Self Damage will be converted to acknowledge Stagger. With this Self-Interrupt system, we have added dozens of new recovery animations that harness a ninja-like recovery experience. By pressing ‘Jump’ at the correct time, you can execute a ninja-skill-based knockdown recovery to ALL in-game knockdowns. This ninja recovery window is indicated by a glowing FX on your Warframe. In the original Dev Workshop, we said:
''As a result of this overall systemic change, Weapons with Stagger will be getting approximately a 20% buff in Damage, with any weapons with AOE receiving a 50% Radial Damage Falloff from central impact.'' This is no longer accurate after continued testing. What we are doing now is: No damage buffs have been added, but any weapons with AOE are receiving ~20% increase in Radius. Additionally, AOE weapons are receiving a 90% Radial Damage Falloff from central impact. This means on the very outer section of the explosion Radius 10% of the Damage will be dealt. Tactics will be deadly - aim true, Tenno. ''Why: Several players brought up the history of the Tonkor and we want to make sure we ship this change in a place that’s conservative in its starting point from a balance perspective. The complete removal of Self Damage does change the pace of destruction with some of the game’s most powerful weapons, so we want to make sure we can iterate upwardly instead of releasing a bonanza of explosions with no other choices.'' ;General Changes: *Removed camera shake and color correction for other players in your squad when firing the Kuva Bramma for less eye bleed! {{ver|27.1.2}} *Optimized the Kuva Bramma cluster bombs with and without Mirage’s Hall of Mirrors, to address issues with crashing due to FX overload. *Fixed the Kuva Bramma multi shot sound FX spamming. {{ver|27.1.1}} *Removed the Kuva Bramma from Conclave eligibility due to not being Conclave balanced yet. *Fixed Kuva Bramma explosion and projectile sounds being too loud for non local players. {{ver|27.1}} *Introduced. }} ==See Also== *{{Weapon|Kulstar}}, a secondary launcher with similar functionality. {{WeaponNav}} [[es:Bramma Kuva]] [[fr:Bramma Kuva]] [[Category:Update 27]] [[Category:Kuva Lich Weapons]] [[Category:Bow]] [[Category:Grineer Weapons]] [[Category:Weapons with Passives]] [[uk:Брама-кува]]

The '''Kuva Hind''' is the [[Kuva (Variant)|Kuva]] variant of the {{Weapon|Hind}}, featuring overall higher stats but with slower [[reload speed]]. In addition to its five-round burst and semi-automatic fire, the Kuva Hind sports a fully-automatic fire mode, all of which can be cycled through the [[Alternate Fire]].

==Characteristics==
*This weapon primarily deals {{D|Slash}} damage.
*Has three togglable firing modes: 5-round burst, semi-auto, and full-auto.
**Semi-auto mode consumes 3 ammo per shot.
*Innate {{Pol|Madurai}} polarity.
*Adversary Weapon:
**Comes with an additional bonus {{D|Impact}}, {{D|Heat}}, {{D|Cold}}, {{D|Electricity}}, {{D|Toxin}}, {{D|Magnetic}}, or {{D|Radiation}} damage, based on the Kuva Lich's [[Adversary System/Progenitor|progenitor Warframe]], which increases the listed base damage of the weapon by 25%-60%.
***[[Valence Fusion]] can optionally change the resulting output damage type, and can upgrade the bonus increase (up to 60%).
**[[Polarization|Polarizing]] the weapon increases its max [[rank]] by '''2''', capping at rank '''40''' after '''5''' polarizations, granting the weapon additional mod capacity.
**{{Resource|Elemental Vice}} can be applied to the weapon after it has reached rank 40, allowing the bonus damage type to be swapped freely.
**Listed [[Mastery Rank]] requirement is not enforced - the weapon may theoretically be obtained at any mastery rank by acquiring and vanquishing a Kuva Lich that has this weapon equipped.

{{Advantages|
*Burst-fire mode:
**Highest [[status chance]] of all burst-fire rifles.
*Semi-auto mode:
**Second highest critical chance of all semi-automatic rifles, behind {{Weapon|Kuva Chakkhurr}}.
}}

{{Disadvantages|
*Burst-fire mode:
**Tied with {{Weapon|Burston}} and {{Weapon|Hind}} for the lowest base damage per bullet of all burst-fire rifles.
**Linearly less efficient – sometimes a target may only die with six bullets, which requires an entire second burst to be fired, or a change to Fire Mode.
*Semi-auto mode:
**Tied with {{Weapon|Hind}} and {{Weapon|Nagantaka}} for the third slowest [[fire rate]] of all semi-automatic rifles, after {{Weapon|Grinlok}}/{{Weapon|Prisma Grinlok}} and {{Weapon|Kuva Chakkhurr}}.
}}
